quest.title: Should You Be Trapped in a Windless Land
quest.description: Jack returns home satisfied after a round of adventure. But Venti finds Stanley's behavior odd, and decides to investigate further...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x500, Primogem x60, Mora x31125, Teachings of Ballad x5, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.title: Should You Be Trapped in a Windless Land

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hans Archibald?

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: Stanley... Stanley...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: You know, I'm glad I actually had the chance to come down here today.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: The tavern isn't overcrowded, and I couldn't be in a better mood.

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: Tell me, Stanley... Tell me what should I do...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Why does he keep repeating his own name?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could there be another person called Stanley?

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: *sobs* Oh, Stanley...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: It should have been me! I should have been the one to die in the Mare Jivari that day... Why won't your spirit come and stop me from using your name? Why, Stanley, why?

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: If only you hadn't had to save a rookie like me, you would have never died in that windless corner of the world...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: You were a renowned adventurer, destined to become a legend one day... But now... that'll never happen, because your life was cut short— and all because of a worthless tag-along...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Does anyone get what's going on here?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: ...I think our friend really did make it to the Mare Jivari. And I think the tragedy he encountered there was real, too.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But the real adventurer, the real Stanley — that was his partner. Not him.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: The real Stanley is the one who died to save our "Stanley."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait... So the only reason our Stanley is called Stanley in the first place is because he stole the other Stanley's name?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I fear that may be the case.

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: Stanley, for so many years I've lived in fear... fear that Mondstadt will forget all about you... So I tell your adventure stories at every opportunity...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: Mondstadt must remember: Stanley reached the center of the Mare Jivari... He's the greatest adventurer there ever was, and he lives on!

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: Stanley will never die, because... I am Stanley! I... am Stanley...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: I'm sorry, Stanley... I'm getting too old... now...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: *sigh* ...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: Are you guys planning on eavesdropping much longer?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yikes! We're busted!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Surely not. Even I've never heard tell of a second Stanley.

talks.objective: Try to make conversation with Stanley

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: *sigh* Go away. Save your questions, just... leave me in peace.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: Leave, now! Don't make me tell you again!

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Honorary Knight! Venti! And Paimon! I'm so glad you guys are here.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: I've been looking for you everywhere! I wanted to thank you again for helping me find the sword and shield. My parents are finally supporting me!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Oh... Really?

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Yeah, really! They even said they're gonna pay for someone to fix up the Sword of Brilliant Valor and Shield of Magnificent Honor for me, so I can take them out on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: That's wonderful! So, Jack, is this the part where you bid farewell to Mondstadt and set off on your intrepid trip traversing Teyvat?

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: No, not yet. I still don't have what it takes to go too far from home just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Besides, I'm sure Stanley still has a few stories left to tell. Hehe... They're what inspired me to become an adventurer in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: Stanley, I— Oh, you're drunk again...

dialogues.speaker: Jack
dialogues.text: See you tomorrow, then. After your hangover wears off, maybe you can tell me some more of your stories?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Stanley's really fond of that kid, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: *hic* Jack? Jack!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Jack left.

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: Oh, I see... Well, thank you for not telling him about my secret.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Eh? All of a sudden you're facing the facts? That isn't like you...

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: Just now... I couldn't bear to look at him. His adventurer's spirit is so pure... unblemished...

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: I'm just a weary old feckless fraud, but that kid is a brand-new shining star, full of potential... I cannot allow his dreams to be crushed.

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: Stories... Experiences... What's the point of them anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: That's my biggest secret of all. And my biggest fear.

dialogues.speaker: Stanley
dialogues.text: But the one thing I can never forget... is that he died in a windless land, where his spirit can never be recovered!

choices.text: His whole life, he's been drowning in guilt...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Exactly... Even in his memory, the real Stanley isn't the living, breathing friend he knew at all.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Instead, he's become fixed on the image of him as that battle-scarred warrior... and that image has held him captive his entire life.

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: I'm too old... I never let go, but still so much has slipped away...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: I'm completely and utterly worthless!

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: No adventurer should have to go that way... No adventurer ever...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: I... I can't believe it...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: Thank you all! And thank you, Lord Barbatos...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: I'm sorry, it's gonna take me some time to calm back down...

response.speaker: Stanley
response.text: But, I think that... I'm gonna be okay...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah, wonderful! Stanley reconnected with his true self, and Jack can finally go his own way.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: This calls for a celebration! And by celebration, I do of course mean libation!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And by libation, you mean you're not leaving this tavern till you're too drunk to walk, right?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Haha... no. The wine here's too expensive. Jack still owes me some wine though — he promised me a rare vintage in exchange for helping him out, remember?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: I'll head off to fetch the wine. See you shortly! Let's meet at the <color=#00E1FFFF>usual place</color>.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Where's that supposed to be? Why has Paimon never heard of it? Hey, Tone-Deaf Bard!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey!

choices.text: I think I know where... possibly.
All that remains is this imaginary friend...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: You made it... finally.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just tell us where you mean next time, okay!? We looked everywhere!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph... So. Did you at least manage to find your wine?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Yep! Well, sort of... Jack made it out to be a rare, collectors' edition vintage...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: ...when actually, it's just a half bottle of regular cider.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Ah, this takes me back.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: The first time I saw this view, I hadn't even taken on this form yet.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: It was about twenty-six hundred years ago, before the world had come under the rule of The Seven.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: At that time, Old Mondstadt was ruled by a tyrant, who sealed off the city's perimeter with a ferocious hurricane. Even the birds couldn't get in or out.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Old Mondstadt? Oh, Paimon remembers — nowadays it's known as Stormterror's Lair, right? You mentioned it before!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: That's right. The tyrant of the winds who once ruled from that tower was Decarabian, God of Storms.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Back then, I was but a wisp among the thousand winds. I wasn't a god of anything — I didn't even have a human form...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: I was just a tiny elemental being who lived in the wind, a gentle breeze bringing subtle changes for the better, or tiny seeds of hope.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A tiny elemental being? Without a human form? Venti... do you mean you used to look different than you do now?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Yep. My current form is not so different from the situation with fake Stanley... I took the form of a friend.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So then what?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened to your friend?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Same situation as with Stanley's friend...)

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Say, Paimon, do you wish to hear the next part of the story?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes, of course! The suspense is killing Paimon!

choices.text: Paimon, go pick us a couple of apples.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now's the time you suddenly get a craving for apples? Really?

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Hahaha, getting a little... peckish or something...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Oh, so peckish.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh! Paimon's had it up to here with you!

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Ah... You know, you're so smart it almost makes me uncomfortable sometimes...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: But then, maybe it's right that true friends can tell what the other is thinking.

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: A refreshing drink, a gentle breeze... *sigh* Moments like this always take me back...

response.speaker: Venti
response.text: Back to a song that I first heard from him...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm listening.

choices.text: Paimon, could you fetch us some meat or fish?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Venti's telling his story! What makes you suddenly wanna have a meat feast!?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: In Old Mondstadt transpired the story to be told

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: Stanley...

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: So many years after the fact, it's not even his friend himself that holds him back anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Diluc
dialogues.text: But I for one am confident that the people of Mondstadt will not forget his friend's story.
